Then regenerate hymn_of_divine_unity_for_the_fourth_day_paytan.xml (the conditional at XML line 104 and the header encoding note at line 35) and draft-appendix-semantic-rules.json. notes: Ruling 835 is met. All 29 unsigned parenthesized spans are independent type='marked' conditionals on opensiddur:variant, each with its own URN, in their printed positions. No couplet stands in for another. L6 and L7 stay separate, as do L20/L22 vs L23 and L24 vs L28. L24's descriptive URN is distinct from L28's /50/optional.

Ruling 834 is met. s335 L22 is an optional whole line. Its content drops the printed ')' because the conditional's delimiters stand in for both parentheses. The missing opener is recorded as <choice><sic/><corr>(</corr></choice> inside an English commentary note targeted at that conditional, not in the prayer text, so no delimiter is doubled.

Canonical boundaries are intact. Every canonical stanza milestone sits before and outside its j:conditional, inside the same tei:l. The null additions L6 and L24 have no milestone and come after bare terminators that sit outside the previous line's scope. L24's tei:seg/@source=/50 encloses both conditional pairs. The /53→/50→/54 order and the single /50 corresp on L28 are as approved and were not reopened.

The nesting is correct. In L24 the outer pair (…_optional_49_0_0) and the inner Divine Name pair (…_49_0_0_divine_name) are both children of the tei:seg. The inner pair lies inside the outer range, and its j:divineName sits within the inner scope. The parentheses around יְיָ were removed from the neighbouring text without losing any other characters.

All seven נ״א alternates are tei:choice elements with two j:option children. Main readings are verbatim and pointed; alternates are as printed, with points only where the source has them. Each choice's corresp carries a /main_reading or /alternate_reading condition URN. s330 L26 leaves וְרוֹחַב outside the choice. s337 L17's colon follows the choice, and the header encoding note documents this.

Each annotation appears once in rendered material: one Hebrew commentary note per choice, targeted at it, keeping the printed parentheses (and the colon for s337). The same strings also appear in English-tagged tei:note[@type='encoding'] elements in the header. Under the guideline those notes stay in the XML and are not printed, so this is not rendered duplication. Optional cleanup: reword the header notes to refer to the xml:id instead of repeating the Hebrew, or mark the Hebrew with xml:lang. They also read as build instructions ('preserve … once') rather than descriptions of the encoding.

Wording: the guideline says marked scopes get the exporter's standard delimiters (brackets or a rule), not necessarily parentheses. The L22 note's 'Supplied delimiter: (' and the header's 'generated conditional delimiters supply its display' are accurate about the source error, but may not match what is actually rendered. Optional rewording only.

L24's name 'levaddo_hu_veniflaot_gedolot' romanizes correctly. Its words also match L28's apart from the optional Divine Name, but it is still a distinct, non-numeric condition URN without a project suffix, which is all that is required.

Raw source text is not modified: changes are confined to fragment fields and post-processing of the generated tree. No English project is produced. All 12 modules appear in draft-schema-report.json as schema-valid. This review covers the draft semantics only, not source, assembly, export or batch acceptance. No edits were made.
